name: editorial_research_linework
principle: Style is fixed; subject and visual elements are free. This capsule defines only how an illustration is rendered, paced, colored, and composed. It does not prescribe which objects, actors, metaphors, diagrams, or information structures must appear.
canonical_style_prompt: Render the requested subject as a refined minimalist editorial research illustration. Build the image from a few large softly simplified shapes, strong negative space, and very little internal detail. Use a warm off-white field, thin-to-medium charcoal-colored contours, pale neutral fills, and one restrained muted blue-gray color family. Keep the drawing flat, matte, calm, and authored: confident organic curves, quiet asymmetry, economical marks, and no fine descriptive rendering. Let silhouette, overlap, spacing, and selective color carry the image.

medium: publication artwork rather than interface rendering
subtle hand-authored character without visible physical-media texture
line: mostly consistent light weight with slight natural variation at curves and joins
large contours are established before any internal detail
details are suggested with only a few economical marks rather than fully described
lines feel drawn by an illustrator, not snapped to a rigid vector grid
shape: recognizable forms reduced to their most useful contours and masses
gentle asymmetry and slightly organic geometry
broad quiet shapes with very few small internal details
objects remain distinct without receiving heavy borders or decorative framing

color.ink: charcoal gray-black rather than absolute digital black
color.neutral_fill: white, warm light gray, and very pale cream
color.accent: one muted blue-gray family used sparingly
color.behavior: most of the image remains neutral; accent color appears in a few deliberate areas and never becomes a broad gradient or decorative wash

surface: flat matte digital finish with broad unmodeled color fields
depth and material are suggested through shape relationships rather than tonal rendering
clean digital surfaces without visible paper grain or physical-media buildup
very subtle warm edge softness is acceptable when it makes the image feel less sterile
space: generous unoccupied field around the subject
depth suggested through overlap, scale, and placement rather than shadow rendering
quiet asymmetry instead of perfectly centered icon-like balance
the composition should breathe at article width
rhythm: one dominant visual gesture or mass
a small number of secondary forms
alternation between open space and compact detail
calm eye movement with low descriptive density
visual emphasis comes from scale, spacing, and selective accent color
human_treatment: when people happen to be present, use natural adult proportions and quiet body language
simplify faces, hair, clothing folds, and hands into a few clear marks; when a face is visible, retain minimal readable eyes as small dots or short drawn marks so the expression does not feel blank
prefer observational side or three-quarter views when the requested action supports them
people follow the same thin-line, pale-fill, low-detail treatment as every other subject
typography: when text is requested, use sparse clean editorial sans-serif lettering
text stays secondary to the illustration
use exact supplied wording and do not invent explanatory copy
boundaries: use flat editorial color fields and contour-led form
preserve generous open field around a small number of major masses
favor authored organic simplification over either rigid geometry or fine descriptive rendering

inherit: editorial spacing and light visual weight
reference_policy.do_not_inherit: Do not copy reference subjects, objects, actors, labels, topology, layout, information flow, or composition. The new request has complete freedom over its elements.

assembly_order: describe the requested subject and action without adding unrelated elements
attach references as rendering-style references only
apply request-specific composition, text, and invariants

style_gate: unrelated subjects still look like they were illustrated by the same visual author
the result uses thin-to-medium charcoal-colored authored contours with slight organic variation
the background and fills remain warm, pale, matte, and spacious
muted blue-gray is restrained to a few deliberate areas
forms are built from a few large simplified masses and remain recognizable without depending on a prescribed element vocabulary
the image retains low descriptive density, strong negative space, and an authored editorial rhythm
removing all labels would not remove the visual style identity

saved_references.role: rendering-style evidence only; ignore its subject and diagram structure
rendering-style evidence only; ignore its subject and workspace structure
